You are already doing all of this work, across a manufacturing system, a quality system, a maintenance system, a requirements tool, and the spreadsheets are filling every gap between them. Epsilon3 is where that work runs on one record instead of many.
From design through sustainment, one system holds the program together through every phase, team, and revision.

The operator sees the current revision in real time. The engineer pulls a part's full history in a click. The director sees deviation rates and quality across every program. The auditor sees the whole trail immediately.
From the drawing through the build, the test, the deployment, the field event, the repair. Pull on any part of the thread and the program comes with it.

Every suggestion arrives as a proposal you accept or reject, not something you discover after the fact. That's a deliberate break from the agentic tools flooding this market, and it's why our customers actually turn AI on. Underneath, it's grounded in your own operating record:
procedures, runs, sign-offs, deviations, test data, telemetry

"Has this valve ever failed checkout?" "What changed between Rev 12 and Rev 14?" Ask across every program you've run and get an answer cited to the exact step, signature, and reading it came from, instead of six people and an afternoon.
It proposes. You accept.

A schedule resequence, a procedure revision, a flagged inconsistency. Each one surfaces as a suggestion you approve or dismiss right where you’re working. Nothing applies itself, and every proposal leaves an audit trail whether you take it or not.
Productive right away.

Onboarding agents walk a new team through configuration and answer from documentation that’s always current. The setup that used to take weeks takes under an hour, and the people who join in year three get the same answers as the people who built it.

Your data is not used to train models. Each call carries context for a single decision and then forgets it. Model-agnostic by architecture: we swap in better models as they ship, and on-prem or classified programs bring their own, including models you've tuned yourself.
